title: Eiffel Tower
text: The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower in Paris, France. It was completed in 1889 and stands 330 metres tall including antennas. It was the tallest man-made structure in the world until 1930.

title: Mount Everest
text: Mount Everest is Earth's highest mountain above sea level, located in the Himalayas. Its summit sits at 8849 metres. It was first summited in 1953 by Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary.

title: Speed of light
text: The speed of light in a vacuum is exactly 299792458 metres per second. It is a fundamental physical constant denoted c.

title: Great Wall of China
text: The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications built across the historical northern borders of China. Its best-known sections were built by the Ming dynasty between 1368 and 1644. Estimates of its total length reach about 21196 kilometres.

title: Golden Gate Bridge
text: The Golden Gate Bridge is a suspension bridge spanning the Golden Gate strait in San Francisco. It opened in 1937. Its main span is 1280 metres long and its towers rise 227 metres above the water.

title: Apollo 11
text: Apollo 11 was the spaceflight that first landed humans on the Moon, on 20 July 1969. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin spent about 21 hours on the lunar surface while Michael Collins orbited above.

title: Pacific Ocean
text: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest of Earth's oceans, covering about 165250000 square kilometres. Its deepest point, the Challenger Deep, is roughly 10935 metres below sea level.

title: Python programming language
text: Python is a high-level programming language created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991. Version 3.0 was released in 2008. It emphasises readability and uses significant indentation.

title: Amazon River
text: The Amazon River in South America is the largest river by discharge volume of water in the world. It is about 6400 kilometres long, making it either the longest or second-longest river depending on the measurement method.

title: Statue of Liberty
text: The Statue of Liberty is a colossal neoclassical sculpture on Liberty Island in New York Harbor, dedicated in 1886. From ground level to the tip of the torch it measures 93 metres; the statue itself is 46 metres.

title: Empire State Building
text: The Empire State Building is an Art Deco skyscraper in Midtown Manhattan, New York City. It was completed in 1931. It stands 443 metres tall to the tip of its antenna and 381 metres to the roof, and it was the world's tallest building for nearly 40 years.

title: Burj Khalifa
text: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, is the tallest structure and building in the world. It opened in 2010 and reaches 828 metres in height with more than 160 storeys.

title: CN Tower
text: The CN Tower is a concrete communications and observation tower in Toronto, Canada. Completed in 1976, it stands 553 metres tall and was the world's tallest free-standing structure for over three decades.

title: Space Needle
text: The Space Needle is an observation tower in Seattle, Washington, built for the 1962 World's Fair. It is 184 metres tall and was designed to withstand high winds and earthquakes.

title: Willis Tower
text: Willis Tower, formerly the Sears Tower, is a 108-storey skyscraper in Chicago, Illinois. It was completed in 1973 and rises 442 metres to the roof. It held the title of world's tallest building for nearly 25 years.

title: Gateway Arch
text: The Gateway Arch is a monument in St. Louis, Missouri, clad in stainless steel and built in the form of a weighted catenary. Completed in 1965, it stands 192 metres tall, the same as its span at ground level.

title: Washington Monument
text: The Washington Monument is an obelisk on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., built to commemorate George Washington. Construction finished in 1884 and the structure is 169 metres tall, making it the world's tallest stone structure.

title: Elizabeth Tower
text: Elizabeth Tower, commonly known after its great bell Big Ben, stands at the north end of the Palace of Westminster in London. It was completed in 1859 and is 96 metres tall.

title: Leaning Tower of Pisa
text: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is the freestanding bell tower of Pisa Cathedral in Italy, famous for its near-four-degree lean. Construction was completed in 1372 and the tower is about 57 metres tall on its high side.

title: Christ the Redeemer
text: Christ the Redeemer is an Art Deco statue of Jesus Christ atop Corcovado mountain in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. It was completed in 1931. The statue itself is 30 metres tall and stands on an 8-metre pedestal.

title: Tokyo Tower
text: Tokyo Tower is a communications and observation tower in the Shiba-koen district of Tokyo, Japan. Completed in 1958 and painted white and international orange, it is 333 metres tall, slightly taller than the Eiffel Tower that inspired it.

title: Petronas Towers
text: The Petronas Towers in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, are twin skyscrapers connected by a skybridge. Completed in 1998, each tower is 452 metres tall, and together they were the tallest buildings in the world until 2004.

title: One World Trade Center
text: One World Trade Center is the main building of the rebuilt World Trade Center complex in Lower Manhattan, New York City. Completed in 2013, its height of 541 metres is a deliberate reference to the year 1776.

title: The Shard
text: The Shard is a pyramid-shaped skyscraper in Southwark, London, designed by Renzo Piano. It was completed in 2012 and stands 310 metres tall, making it the tallest building in the United Kingdom.

title: Taipei 101
text: Taipei 101 is a supertall skyscraper in Taipei, Taiwan. Completed in 2004, it is 508 metres tall to its architectural top and held the world's-tallest-building title until the Burj Khalifa opened.

title: Chrysler Building
text: The Chrysler Building is an Art Deco skyscraper on the East Side of Manhattan, New York City. Completed in 1930, it is 319 metres tall and was briefly the tallest building in the world before the Empire State Building overtook it.

title: Sydney Opera House
text: The Sydney Opera House is a multi-venue performing arts centre on Sydney Harbour, Australia, known for its series of white shell-like roofs. It was formally opened in 1973. Its highest roof shell rises about 65 metres above sea level.
